A LEGACY TRACE FORM INSIDE A STRING LITERAL, in a test's own span. Rust has masked string contents before matching legacy forms since the mask was written — `src/symbols/trace.rs` gated it on `SourceLanguage::Rust` and every other language fell through to the raw span. So a Python or TypeScript test that carries tag-shaped text as DATA bound it, and the row read as verified by a test that never touches it. Measured on this fixture at engine `d55c987`: `backed 2/3` with nothing unbacked, which is invented coverage nobody authored. The repair is the mask, not the fixture: the text is a legitimate thing for a test to assert about.

Nothing here was ever misspelled: the declared heading is present and correct, the declared id column is correct, and all three tests bind. FR-065-AC-42 rejected the pair, correctly. The input is still the shape that used to strand rows, and asserting that it mints all four is worth keeping.

Every assertion sits behind a narrowing guard, so an input that does not enter it passes unchecked. TC-1596 was green while checking 2.3% of its samples.

THE GUARD IS GONE AND NOTHING ELSE MOVED. The same test, the same tag, the same two documents, the same one bound symbol — the assertion is simply reached on every input instead of only on the ones that enter an `if let`. Every coverage count is identical to its partner's by design: `backed 1`, `total 3`, `binding_census rust 1/1`, which is precisely the payload the failure case published for months while asserting nothing about its own defect. The whole separation is `suspicions`, which is the channel neither reader could name until agent-ix/quire-rs#358. This is also the harder control: a detector written as "a test whose body contains a conditional" fires here and is wrong, because the question is whether an assertion can be SKIPPED, not whether a branch exists.
